deep.reconstruction:
This page continues the catalogue on p.154 of 'balayages élémentaires des positions relatives', meaning elementary sweeps of the relative position of a pseudo-line with respect to a fixed system Σ of pseudo-lines.

Setting: Σ is a configuration (system) of pseudo-lines in the plane. A further curve, drawn as the brown double contour around a green 'median' position, has a relative position with respect to Σ, recorded by which vertices of Σ lie above or below it. An elementary sweep deforms the curve, along the ↑ and ↓ arrows, across a small set of vertices of Σ. The hypothesis is that no other vertices or traces of lines of Σ are met. That is what the annotations 'pas d'autres sommets de Σ ici que a' and '... que b, c' say. The pencil fans through the dots are the lines of Σ passing through those vertices.

The drawings on this page:
- Bottom left: a sweep pushing the curve over one vertex upward and one downward, the configuration (I_2) of p.154.
- Bottom middle: a curve pushed up over one vertex and down over two, an asymmetric variant.
- Bottom right: the (I_3) configuration, with vertex a above and b, c below.
- Small sketch under the bottom left: a lens version of the same move.
- Upper right: a zigzag inscribed in a lens, the general (I_n) case announced at the end of p.154 (n odd, asymmetric). The red dots alternate between the upper and lower boundary of the region swept.
- Top: large lens-shaped regions bounded by two red curves through vertices of a triangular grid of pencil lines. These are global sweeps of a curve across many vertices of a near-regular arrangement, decomposed into elementary ones.
- Middle: a curve dipping under a single vertex (the dashed V), and a bump over one vertex with a green intermediate position. These illustrate passing through a 'critical' position.

The page under p.154's statements: for I_1 the move is asymmetric and position 1 is never critical. For I_2 it is symmetric, and 1 is critical iff 2 is. For I_3 it is asymmetric, yet 1 is critical iff 2 is.

Probable purpose: to show that the set of relative positions of a pseudo-line with respect to Σ (equivalently, one-element extensions of the arrangement) is connected by elementary sweeps. A second aim is to control how 'criticality' (likely, being a position realisable through a vertex or extremal) behaves under these moves. The next page turns to the reflection-like generators σ0, σ1, σ2 acting on flags (D0, ±β*, ±ω*), i.e. the symmetry group of a local configuration.
errors: No explicit claims beyond the hypothesis annotations, so nothing to check. The meaning of 'p.r. critique' is not defined on this page; its interpretation here is conjectural.

ideas.what: Elementary sweeps of a pseudo-line across one, two, three or n vertices of an arrangement Σ, used to connect relative positions
ideas.modern_name: Flips / mutations in the space of one-element extensions of a rank-3 oriented matroid; topological sweep of pseudoline arrangements
ideas.usually_credited_to: Ringel (1956) for flips; Goodman–Pollack (1980s) for sweeps; Edelsbrunner–Guibas (1986) for topological sweep; Sturmfels–Ziegler (1993) for extension spaces

ideas.what: Classification of local sweep configurations I_1, I_2, I_3, I_n (zigzag) by symmetry, and whether criticality of position 1 is equivalent to that of position 2
ideas.modern_name: Local moves in the extension graph / cocircuit graph of an oriented matroid

missed.claim: Grothendieck's systematic study of the 'positions relatives' of an extra pseudo-line with respect to a system Σ, and of the elementary sweeps between them, is in substance the study of the extension space of a rank-3 oriented matroid and its connectivity under local moves. It predates or parallels Sturmfels–Ziegler's 'Extension spaces of oriented matroids' (1993) and related work on single-element extensions, and is not cited in that literature.
missed.quote: pas d'autres sommets de Σ ici que a ... b ... c
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: The connectivity and topology of extension spaces is a subtle topic: in higher rank, extension spaces can be disconnected (Mnëv–Ziegler type phenomena). A worked rank-3 analysis with a notion of 'critical' positions could be of historical interest and might give an independent combinatorial treatment.

missed.claim: The general (I_n) zigzag case is only sketched. The notion of critical relative position and its invariance under sweeps ('1 critique ssi 2 l'est') is not carried through to a theorem on this page.
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Only minor importance. It would complete a classification of elementary moves, but comparable results exist in the oriented matroid literature.

deep.surprise_reason: These are sketches of local sweep moves for pseudoline arrangements. They are a notable private parallel to oriented-matroid extension-space work, but contain no stated result going beyond what is known.

Lower-right annotation (struck through near the typescript) reads approximately 'pas d'autres sommets de Σ que b, c' (partly illegible).
The upside-down typescript reads '...E NIVEAU DU SYSTEME MVS/SP 1.3, SERA MIS EN SERVICE SUR LE ... JOUR LE 21 AOUT 1982.' This is recycled computer paper and not mathematical content.
The drawings contain dot labels a, b, c and arrows ↑ ↓ in the I_3 sketches, at both bottom left and bottom right.
